why: Most of the briefs are fine. The builder adds a slugify section. Checks 1, 2 and 4 match their lines, and check 1 uses single-character fills without demanding that fill must be one character. Check 3 is broken, though. Its node script sits inside a double-quoted bash string, so bash turns `'^#+\\s.*\\b'` into `'^#+\s.*\b'`. In a JS string literal, `\s` becomes plain `s` and `\b` becomes a backspace character. The regex then needs a line like "#s" followed by a backspace, which no README heading can match. Every exported function is reported missing and the check exits 1 even when README.md is fully correct. That FAIL condition is stricter than line 3, which must_not item 2 forbids. Check 3 also asks for describing text under each heading. That is a smaller extra demand, but it adds to the same problem.
